before: // SS_done is set from the value about to land, not the current
// one, so the ramp does not finish a step late.
after: // SS_done is set from the value about to land, not the current
// one, so the ramp does not finish a step late.
proposal.description: The SS_done look-ahead is tested on every clock below the target instead of only on the clock the last step lands, so SS_done rises as soon as the ceiling is one count below max_on_limit.
proposal.reason: During S_SS, SS_done goes high a whole step window before the last step lands. The supervisor then moves to S_RUN and holds max_on_counts at max_on_limit-1 instead of max_on_limit.

proposal.description: On the at-target branch SS_done only counts as done when the ceiling already equals the limit, so a ceiling clamped down from above a lowered max_on_limit finishes one clock late.
proposal.reason: If max_on_limit is written below the current ceiling during S_SS, max_on_counts is clamped on the first clock but SS_done stays low until the next clock, so S_SS lasts one clock longer.

proposal.description: Outside S_SS and S_RUN the ceiling is reset to the target max_on_limit (a copy of the clamp line) instead of to the MIN_ON_CNT floor.
proposal.reason: After a hiccup or any return to idle, max_on_counts shows max_on_limit instead of the floor. On the next S_SS the at-target test is true on the first clock, so SS_done asserts at once and the retry starts at full ceiling with no ramp.

proposal.description: The step-window counter advances on the PWM rising edge, while the ceiling step is still taken at the falling edge.
proposal.reason: With cycles_per_step > 1, the counter has already advanced by the first falling edge of S_SS. The first ceiling step therefore comes one switching cycle early, and SS_done comes early too.

proposal.description: The idle re-arm sets the ceiling one count above the MIN_ON_CNT floor, unlike the power-on reset, so a re-ramp starts at the first step instead of the floor.
proposal.reason: After leaving S_RUN or S_SS for hiccup or idle, max_on_counts reads MIN_ON_CNT+1 instead of MIN_ON_CNT. The next soft start begins one count wider and reaches max_on_limit one step window sooner.
